name: setuid
description: The setuid() system call sets the effective user ID of the calling process. If the process is privileged (e.g., has the CAP_SETUID capability), it also sets the real and saved set-user-ID. This allows set-user-ID programs to temporarily drop privileges and potentially regain them securely.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: The new effective user ID to set for the calling process.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: The call would change the caller’s real UID, but there was a temporary failure allocating kernel data structures, or it would exceed the RLIMIT_NPROC resource limit.
The user ID specified in uid is not valid in this user namespace.
The process is not privileged and uid does not match the real UID or saved set-user-ID of the calling process.

bugs: Not fully compatible with 4.4BSD, which sets all real, saved, and effective user IDs.
versions: POSIX.1-2001, SVr4; Linux 2.4 added 32-bit ID support
